instruction.text: Dascha ruft einen australischen Freund ihrer Mutter an. Vervollständige den Dialog.
instruction.sound: Dasha ruft einen australischen Freund ihrer Mutter an. Vervollständige den Dialog.

atoms.b: Hello Archie, can you tell me something interesting about Australia?
Hey Dascha, how are you doing? Of course. Have you ever heard of the ((++Outback Caribbean))?
I'm not sure, what is that?
The Outback is a very large area in Australia. It is characterised by different landscapes. Best known is the orange desert with several mountain ranges.

instruction.text: Welches Bild zeigt das australische Outback? Wähle es aus.

atoms.b: The Outback is very sparsely populated. Its area makes up 90% of Australia but only has about ((++700,000 700_million)) inhabitants. 17% of the population is indigenous.

hint.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>sparsely populated</voice> bedeutet dünn besiedelt

atoms.b: The Outback stretches from the northern to the southern coastline and thus contains different ((++climate_zones heat_waves)). In the north, the climate is rather tropical. The so-called red centre is very dry. Southern regions are likely to be temperate.
I read online that Australia is megadiverse! And where does the Kookaburra live?
atoms.sound: I read online that Australia is mega-diverse! And where does the Kookaburra live?

atoms.b: They are very likely to live in Eastern Australia since they need ((++trees ++the_desert)) to build their ((++nests caves)) in. Why don't we play a little animal-guessing game? I describe an animal and you try to name it.
Sure!
Alright. The first animal has a similar habitat as the Kookaburra because it climbs trees to feed on eucalyptus and hide from predators. Its fur is mostly grey, it has big ears and a big black nose.

instruction.text: Wähle das passende Tier zur Beschreibung aus.

atoms.b: Is that maybe a ((++koala kangaroo))?

Correct! The next animal has a compact head, a stocky body, short legs, and a very short tail. Its eyes and ears are small and the fur is mostly brown. This animal can be found in open and dry regions.

instruction.text: Wähle das passende Tier zur Beschreibung aus.

atoms.b: That is difficult. That also sounds like a koala.
Not quite, although it's related to the koala. It's actually a ((++wombat capybara)). Those animals are very much loved over here.
The last animal is really strange. It has a tail and fur like a beaver, feet like an otter and a beak like a duck. Plus, this animal is an egg-laying mammal living in the water and on land.

hint.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>beak</voice> bedeutet Schnabel. <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>mammal</voice> bedeutet Säugetier

instruction.text: Wähle das passende Tier zur Beschreibung aus.

atoms.b: Oh, I know this one. Is it a ((++platypus beaver))?
Exactly. Two out of three, not bad!
Have you ever been to the Outback?
Of course! Currently, I'm living in Sydney but a few years ago I worked as a volunteer at Uluru – a big mountain in ((++the_Outback Melbourne)).
Is there something special about it?

It is a massive, single mountain in the middle of the ((++desert forest)). It is a sacred place for the Anangu, the Aboriginal people of this region. Have a look at the brochure I just sent you. I got to run now. Cheerio!
Great. Thanks, Archie! Have a good one.
atoms.sound: Great. Thanks Archie! Have a good one.

instruction.text: Lies den Text und entscheide anschließend, ob die Aussage über den Uluru wahr oder falsch ist.

atoms.sound: The Uluru-Kata choota National Park is Aboriginal land. This cultural centre offers the possibility for visitors to learn about the Ah-nangoo, their ancestors and the laws they preserve and liv by. The UNESCO World Heritage Area offers both cultural and natural values. The visitors are welcome to explore the Cultural Centre to learn about the Ah-nangoo as well as to enjoy the beauty and cultural richness of the unique geological formation.

atoms.a: Uluru belongs to the Australian government.
Uluru offers the possibility to learn about Aboriginal culture.
Tourists aren't welcome at Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.
